description: If total assets are \$80000 and total equity is \$35000 what are total liabilities?
explanation: Using the accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Equity so Liabilities = Assets - Equity = \$80000 - \$35000 = \$45000.

description: Which of the following transactions would include a debit to Cash?
explanation: When a customer pays on account Cash is debited because the asset increases. All other options would credit Cash.
choice2: Collecting cash from a customer on account

description: If current assets are \$60000 and current liabilities are \$20000 what is the current ratio?
explanation: Current ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities = \$60000 / \$20000 = 3.0. A ratio above 1 means the company has more current assets than current liabilities.
hint: Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities

description: Which journal entry records the payment of salaries that were previously accrued?
explanation: Salaries were previously accrued by debiting Salaries Expense and crediting Salaries Payable. When paid the liability is debited to eliminate it and Cash is credited.
choice0: Debit Salaries Expense and Credit Cash
choice1: Debit Cash and Credit Salaries Payable
choice2: Debit Salaries Expense and Credit Salaries Payable
choice3: Debit Salaries Payable and Credit Cash

description: Under the FIFO inventory method when prices are rising which result is correct?
explanation: Under FIFO the oldest (lowest cost) inventory is sold first. During rising prices this means COGS is lower and ending inventory value is higher compared to LIFO.
choice0: Higher COGS and lower ending inventory
choice1: Lower COGS and higher ending inventory

description: The net realizable value of accounts receivable equals?
explanation: Net realizable value is the amount of accounts receivable the company actually expects to collect. It equals gross accounts receivable minus the allowance for doubtful accounts.
choice0: Gross accounts receivable minus sales discounts
choice1: Total credit sales minus cash collected
choice2: Gross accounts receivable minus allowance for doubtful accounts

description: A company buys equipment for \$10000 with a salvage value of \$2000 and a 4-year life. What is straight-line annual depreciation?
explanation: Straight-line depreciation = (Cost - Salvage Value) / Useful Life = (\$10000 - \$2000) / 4 = \$8000 / 4 = \$2000 per year.

description: Which of the following would increase gross profit without changing net sales?
explanation: Lower cost of goods sold (COGS) increases gross profit because Gross Profit = Net Sales - COGS. If COGS decreases while sales stay the same gross profit increases.

description: Which of the following best describes working capital?
explanation: Working capital = Current Assets - Current Liabilities. It measures the short-term liquidity of a company.

description: An accrued expense is best described as?
explanation: An accrued expense is one that has been incurred but not yet paid. It creates a liability at the end of the period before cash payment occurs.
choice0: An expense paid before it is incurred
choice1: An expense recorded when cash is paid
choice2: An expense incurred but not yet paid
choice3: A prepaid expense used during the period

description: If a company debits Accounts Receivable and credits Revenue what type of transaction occurred?
explanation: Debiting Accounts Receivable and crediting Revenue records a sale on credit. The company earned revenue but has not yet received cash.
choice1: Cash was collected from a customer
choice3: An asset was purchased on credit

description: A company performs services in December but receives payment in January. Under accrual accounting revenue is recorded in?
explanation: Under accrual accounting revenue is recognized when earned - when the service is performed - not when payment is received. So revenue is recorded in December.
choice1: February at the next accounting period
choice3: December when the service is performed

description: Which of the following items appears on the statement of cash flows but NOT on the income statement?
explanation: Capital expenditures (buying equipment) appear only in the investing section of the cash flow statement - not on the income statement.

description: The materiality principle allows companies to?
explanation: The materiality principle states that for immaterial (trivial) amounts strict adherence to GAAP is not required since the impact on financial statements is negligible.
choice0: Omit major items from financial statements
choice1: Record assets at market value rather than cost
choice2: Expense minor items immediately even if they technically should be capitalized
choice3: Defer all expenses to future periods

description: When merchandise is purchased on account the journal entry is?
explanation: Purchasing merchandise on account increases Inventory (asset - debit) and creates an obligation to pay (Accounts Payable - credit the liability).
choice0: Debit Inventory and Credit Accounts Payable
choice1: Debit Accounts Payable and Credit Inventory

description: A company has net income of \$30000 and net sales of \$150000. What is the net profit margin?
explanation: Net Profit Margin = Net Income / Net Sales = \$30000 / \$150000 = 0.20 or 20%.
hint: Net Profit Margin = Net Income / Net Sales

description: Treasury stock (shares repurchased by the company) appears on the balance sheet as?
explanation: Treasury stock is a contra-equity account. It reduces stockholders equity and is listed as a deduction within the equity section.

description: What is the journal entry to record depreciation expense?
explanation: You debit Depreciation Expense (increases the expense) and credit Accumulated Depreciation (a contra-asset that reduces the book value of the asset).
choice0: Debit Asset and Credit Depreciation Expense
choice1: Debit Depreciation Expense and Credit Cash
choice2: Debit Depreciation Expense and Credit Accumulated Depreciation
choice3: Debit Accumulated Depreciation and Credit Depreciation Expense

description: At year-end a company owes \$5000 in interest that has not been paid. What entry is required?
explanation: An interest obligation that exists but has not been paid is an accrued liability. You debit Interest Expense and credit Interest Payable.
choice0: Debit Interest Expense and Credit Interest Payable
choice1: Debit Interest Payable and Credit Cash
choice2: Debit Cash and Credit Interest Expense
choice3: Debit Interest Expense and Credit Cash

description: Accumulated depreciation on the balance sheet is classified as?
explanation: Accumulated Depreciation is a contra-asset account. It is listed as a deduction from the related asset to show net book value.

description: Which inventory method assumes the most recently purchased goods are sold first?
explanation: LIFO stands for Last-In First-Out. It assumes the most recently purchased inventory is sold first. This is the opposite of FIFO.

description: A company pays \$12000 on January 1 for a 12-month insurance policy. Under accrual accounting how much insurance expense is recorded in January?
explanation: Under accrual accounting only 1 month of coverage (1 / 12 of \$12000 = \$1000) is used in January so only \$1000 is recognized as expense.

description: Bad debt expense is recorded under the allowance method when?
explanation: Under the allowance method bad debt expense is estimated and recorded at the end of each period - before any specific account is identified as uncollectible.
choice0: An estimate of uncollectible accounts is made at period end
choice1: A specific customer account is written off
choice2: A customer pays a previously written-off account

description: If a company has total debt of \$200000 and total equity of \$400000 what is the debt-to-equity ratio?
explanation: Debt-to-Equity Ratio = Total Debt / Total Equity = \$200000 / \$400000 = 0.5.

description: Intangible assets include which of the following?
explanation: Intangible assets are non-physical long-term assets with economic value. Patents and trademarks are intangible. Equipment and buildings are tangible. Accounts receivable is a current asset.

description: When a company issues common stock for cash the journal entry is?
explanation: Issuing stock for cash increases Cash (asset - debit) and increases Common Stock (equity - credit).
choice0: Debit Common Stock and Credit Cash
choice1: Debit Cash and Credit Retained Earnings
choice2: Debit Cash and Credit Common Stock
choice3: Debit Revenue and Credit Common Stock

description: On a multi-step income statement what appears between gross profit and operating income?
explanation: On a multi-step income statement: Gross Profit - Operating Expenses = Operating Income. Operating expenses appear between gross profit and operating income.

description: Deferred (unearned) revenue arises when?
explanation: Deferred revenue is created when a company receives cash before it earns the revenue by performing the service or delivering the product.
choice0: A company records revenue before the sale is made
choice1: A customer has not yet paid for services performed
choice2: An expense is paid in advance
choice3: Cash is received before the service is performed

description: A company receives a \$500 utility bill but does not pay it immediately. What is the correct journal entry?
explanation: Receiving a utility bill creates an expense (Utilities Expense - debit) and a liability (Accounts Payable - credit).
choice0: Debit Cash and Credit Utilities Expense
choice1: Debit Utilities Expense and Credit Accounts Payable
choice2: Debit Utilities Payable and Credit Utilities Expense
choice3: Debit Accounts Payable and Credit Cash

description: Which depreciation method results in higher depreciation expense in the early years of an asset's life?
explanation: The double-declining-balance method is an accelerated method that applies twice the straight-line rate to book value. It results in higher depreciation in earlier years.

description: A company has gross profit of \$90000 and net sales of \$300000. What is the gross profit margin?
explanation: Gross Profit Margin = Gross Profit / Net Sales = \$90000 / \$300000 = 0.30 or 30%.
hint: Gross Profit Margin = Gross Profit / Net Sales

description: Which of the following is classified as a financing activity on the cash flow statement?
explanation: Borrowing money by issuing a note payable is a financing activity. Buying equipment is investing. Collecting from customers and paying suppliers are operating activities.
choice3: Borrowing money by issuing a note payable

description: Under the weighted average cost method inventory cost is calculated as?
explanation: The weighted average cost method divides the total cost of goods available for sale by the total number of units available.
choice0: Cost of the first units purchased
choice1: Cost of the last units purchased
choice2: Total cost divided by total units available

description: The full disclosure principle requires that?
explanation: The full disclosure principle requires that all material information that could affect user decisions be disclosed in the financial statements and notes.
choice0: All transactions be recorded in real time
choice2: All material information that could affect decisions be disclosed in financial statements
choice3: Companies report detailed information about every employee

description: Which of the following is classified as a long-term (non-current) asset?
explanation: Property and equipment are long-term assets used over many years. Cash, accounts receivable, and inventory are current assets.

description: To close revenue accounts at the end of the period you would?
explanation: Temporary accounts are closed at period-end. To close a revenue account with a credit balance you debit the revenue account and credit Income Summary.
choice0: Debit Income Summary and Credit Retained Earnings
choice1: Debit Revenue and Credit Retained Earnings
choice3: Debit Revenue and Credit Income Summary

description: When a company takes advantage of a purchase discount the cash paid is?
explanation: A purchase discount reduces the amount paid for inventory. Paying within the discount period means paying less than the full invoice price.
choice0: Equal to the full invoice price
choice1: Less than the full invoice price
choice2: More than the full invoice price
choice3: The same regardless of when payment is made

description: A prepaid expense is initially recorded as?
explanation: When an expense is paid in advance it is recorded as an asset (prepaid expense) because it represents a future economic benefit.

description: Under a single-step income statement all revenues are grouped together and then?
explanation: A single-step income statement groups all revenues together and all expenses together. Total revenues minus total expenses = net income.
choice0: All expenses are deducted in one step to get net income
choice2: Operating and non-operating items are separated
choice3: Cost of goods sold is subtracted first

description: If accounts receivable is \$50000 and net credit sales are \$300000 what is the accounts receivable turnover?
explanation: Accounts Receivable Turnover = Net Credit Sales / Accounts Receivable = \$300000 / \$50000 = 6. This means the company collects its receivables balance 6 times per year.
hint: AR Turnover = Net Credit Sales / Accounts Receivable

description: Under straight-line depreciation the book value of an asset at the end of its useful life should equal?
explanation: Under straight-line depreciation the asset is depreciated down to its estimated salvage value by the end of its useful life.

description: In the indirect method of preparing the operating section of the cash flow statement depreciation is?
explanation: Depreciation is a non-cash expense deducted on the income statement. To reconcile net income to operating cash flows we add depreciation back because no cash was actually paid.
choice1: Added to net income only if it exceeds \$1000

description: A company pays a \$3000 dividend to shareholders. How does this affect the accounting equation?
explanation: Dividends reduce retained earnings (equity decreases) and reduce cash (asset decreases). The equation remains balanced because both sides decrease by the same amount.

description: Which accounting principle supports recording an asset at its original cost rather than its inflated current value?
explanation: The cost principle (historical cost) requires that assets be recorded and reported at their original acquisition cost.

description: A company debits Rent Expense and credits Prepaid Rent. What accounting event occurred?
explanation: Crediting Prepaid Rent reduces the asset (the prepaid has been used up). Debiting Rent Expense records the cost of the period used. This is an adjusting entry.
choice1: Prepaid rent was used up and expensed
choice3: Future rent was paid in advance

description: Which of the following would be found in the stockholders equity section of a balance sheet?
explanation: Retained Earnings is part of stockholders equity. Notes Payable is a liability. Accounts Receivable is an asset. Unearned Revenue is a liability.

description: Which inventory costing method is NOT permitted under IFRS?
explanation: LIFO is prohibited under IFRS because it can distort inventory values and income. FIFO, Weighted Average, and Specific Identification are all acceptable under IFRS.

description: Which basis of accounting better matches revenues with the expenses incurred to earn them?
explanation: Accrual basis records revenues when earned and expenses when incurred regardless of cash flow. This provides better matching than the cash basis.

description: When a specific customer account is written off under the allowance method the entry is?
explanation: Writing off a specific account reduces Accounts Receivable and reduces the Allowance for Doubtful Accounts. Bad Debt Expense is NOT recorded at write-off under the allowance method.
choice0: Debit Bad Debt Expense and Credit Accounts Receivable
choice1: Debit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts and Credit Accounts Receivable
choice2: Debit Accounts Receivable and Credit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts
choice3: Debit Bad Debt Expense and Credit Allowance for Doubtful Accounts

description: A company purchases land for \$75000 cash. How does this transaction affect the accounting equation?
explanation: Buying land for cash swaps one asset (cash) for another asset (land). Total assets remain the same. Neither liabilities nor equity are affected.
choice2: Assets are unchanged (one asset replaces another)
